content: The following studies provide insights into various treatments for chronic low back pain: 1. Dohner et al. conducted a blinded randomized clinical trial to evaluate the effects of electroacupuncture and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) on chronic nonspecific low back pain. The study, published in the Muscles, Ligaments, and Tendons Journal in 2021, demonstrated the potential benefits of these interventions in managing pain and improving functionality. 2. Haake et al. performed the German Acupuncture Trials (GERAC), a multicenter, blinded, randomized trial with three groups, to assess acupuncture's efficacy for chronic low back pain. Published in Archives of Internal Medicine in 2007, the study highlighted acupuncture as a promising treatment option. 3. Huang et al. investigated the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for chronic discogenic sciatica in a randomized controlled trial comparing real acupuncture to sham acupuncture. The findings, published in Pain Medicine in 2019, supported acupuncture's role in reducing pain and improving outcomes. 4. Kerr et al. conducted a blinded randomized controlled trial to explore acupuncture's effectiveness in managing chronic low back pain. Published in the Clinical Journal of Pain in 2003, the study provided evidence for acupuncture's therapeutic benefits. 5. Kim et al. examined the relationship between reduced tactile acuity in chronic low back pain and structural neuroplasticity in the primary somatosensory cortex. Their 2020 study in NeuroImage demonstrated that acupuncture therapy could modulate these changes and improve symptoms. 6. Kong et al. compared electroacupuncture to sham treatment in a randomized clinical trial to assess changes in pain severity among adults with chronic low back pain. Published in JAMA Network Open in 2020, the study confirmed electroacupuncture's effectiveness in pain management. 7. Li et al. explored the combination of core stability training and acupuncture for chronic nonspecific low back pain in a prospective randomized controlled trial. Published in Zhen Ci Yan Jiu in 2022, the study highlighted the synergistic effects of these interventions. 8. Martín-Corrales et al. evaluated the benefits of adding gluteal dry needling to a four-week physical exercise program for chronic low back pain patients. Their randomized clinical trial, published in Pain Medicine in 2020, demonstrated improved outcomes with the combined approach. 9. Meng et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess acupuncture's effectiveness in older patients with chronic low back pain. Published in Rheumatology (Oxford) in 2003, the study supported acupuncture as a viable treatment for this population. 10. Molsberger et al. investigated whether acupuncture improves orthopedic management of chronic low back pain in a randomized, blinded, controlled trial with three months of follow-up. Published in Pain in 2002, the study provided evidence for acupuncture's role in enhancing treatment outcomes. 11. Moslemi and Farokhi examined the effects of electroacupuncture on pain, functional disability, and ultrasonographic changes in the gluteus maximus muscle in patients with chronic nonspecific low back pain. Their findings, published in Koomesh in 2020, highlighted electroacupuncture's therapeutic potential. 12. Pan et al. studied the effects of combining acupuncture with sling exercise training for lumbar disc herniation in a clinical trial. Published in the Journal of New Chinese Medicine in 2019, the study demonstrated significant improvements in pain and lumbar function. 13. Ren et al. conducted a clinical study on the analgesic effects of acupuncture based on meridian-tendon dialectical theory in chronic low back pain. Published in the Chinese Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine in 2021, the study supported acupuncture's efficacy in pain relief. 14. Shi et al. observed the treatment of nonspecific low back pain using acupuncture based on meridian theory. Published in the Journal of Practical Traditional Chinese Internal Medicine in 2021, the study confirmed acupuncture's effectiveness in improving pain and function. 15. Sung et al. evaluated the efficacy and safety of thread embedding acupuncture combined with traditional acupuncture for chronic low back pain in a randomized, assessor-blinded, multicenter clinical trial. Published in Medicine in 2020, the study demonstrated significant benefits of the combined approach. 16. Tabatabaiee et al. investigated the effects of ultrasound-guided dry needling on pain in patients with piriformis syndrome. Published in Muscle Nerve in 2019, the study highlighted the effectiveness of this technique in reducing pain. 17. Ushinohama et al. assessed the impact of a single session of ear acupuncture on pain intensity and postural control in individuals with chronic low back pain. Published in the Brazilian Journal of Physical Therapy in 2016, the study demonstrated immediate benefits of ear acupuncture. 18. Wang et al. observed the efficacy of acupuncture for lumbar intervertebral disc herniation in a study published in Shanghai Journal of Acu-Mox in 2020. The findings supported acupuncture's role in pain management and functional improvement. 19. Weiss et al. conducted a prospective, randomized, controlled trial to evaluate acupuncture's effectiveness and acceptance in patients with chronic low back pain. Published in the Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine in 2013, the study confirmed acupuncture's therapeutic value. 20. Witt et al. performed a pragmatic randomized trial to evaluate the clinical and economic effectiveness of acupuncture for chronic low back pain. Published in the American Journal of Epidemiology in 2006, the study demonstrated acupuncture's cost-effectiveness and clinical benefits. These studies collectively highlight the diverse approaches and evidence supporting acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and related therapies in managing chronic low back pain.
